title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Ten named destinations along the walkable downtown and lakefront corridors near Lake Forest College, each paired with one documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Study a Landmark Shopping Square
cards.subtitle: Market Square at North Western Avenue
cards.notes: Enter from North Western Avenue and examine the clock tower, arcades, central green, and mixed architectural details documented by its official history.
cards.short_summary: A compact architecture-focused stop in Lake Forest’s historic downtown core.
cards.evidence_claim: Market Square opened in 1916, faces Western Avenue, and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor common areas are publicly approachable; individual shops and events maintain separate access policies.

cards.title: Settle In with Books and Courtyards
cards.subtitle: East Deerpath Road corridor
cards.notes: Walk east on Deerpath Road, browse the public collection, then step into the rehabilitated courtyards to see their stone paving and landscaping.
cards.short_summary: A civic reading stop with restored outdoor courtyards beside Deerpath Road.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest Library is located at 360 East Deerpath Road and offers library services, programs, and restored courtyards.
cards.access_notes: Public library access applies during posted hours; some programs require registration and borrowing privileges may require a card.

cards.title: Check the Arts Calendar
cards.subtitle: East Illinois Road at McKinley Road
cards.notes: Turn onto East Illinois Road and check Gorton’s calendar before entering; the historic center presents films, performances, classes, and community events.
cards.short_summary: A multidisciplinary arts destination housed in a former school near the station.
cards.evidence_claim: Gorton Center occupies 400 East Illinois Road and presents live entertainment, films, classes, and cultural programs for all ages.
cards.access_notes: Building access depends on scheduled programs and events; registration or tickets may be required for particular offerings.

cards.entity_name: History Center of Lake Forest-Lake Bluff
cards.title: Trace Local Stories and Maps
cards.subtitle: East Deerpath Road at Washington Road
cards.notes: Continue along East Deerpath to the museum, explore its exhibition galleries, and arrange ahead if you want to consult maps or photographs in the archives.
cards.short_summary: A community museum connecting local exhibits with an appointment-based research archive.
cards.evidence_claim: The History Center is at 509 East Deerpath and provides exhibition galleries, interactive exhibits, and research access to maps, photographs, books, and archives.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit — History Center Lake Forest-Lake Bluff
cards.access_notes: Visit during posted museum hours; the Research Center is appointment-only, and visitors must check in at the museum desk.

cards.title: Walk the Lakefront Paths
cards.subtitle: North Lake Road corridor
cards.notes: Follow North Lake Road to the lakefront, use the stairs or boardwalk for beach access, and check posted water conditions before approaching the water.
cards.short_summary: A Lake Michigan stop with beach, bluff-top parkland, paths, and a fishing pier.
cards.evidence_claim: Forest Park Beach at 801 North Lake Road includes a beach, grass areas, walking paths, sheltered pavilions, a fishing pier, and seasonal lifeguards.
cards.source_title: Forest Park Beach — Lake Forest Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: Park hours are 6:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. Nonresidents face a beach-access fee in season; parking is restricted. Follow current swimming and youth-supervision rules.

cards.title: Catch the Union Pacific North Line
cards.subtitle: North Western Avenue rail corridor
cards.notes: Approach the station from North Western Avenue and consult Metra’s current schedule before using the Union Pacific North line toward Chicago or Kenosha.
cards.short_summary: The downtown rail stop linking the college’s walkable orbit with Chicago and the North Shore.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College identifies the downtown Lake Forest Metra stop on the Union Pacific North line as a ten-minute walk from campus.
cards.access_notes: Check Metra’s current timetable and fares before travel; not every train necessarily stops at every station.

cards.title: Browse an Independent Bookshop
cards.subtitle: North Western Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk the North Western Avenue storefronts and browse the shop’s books, stationery, and gifts; check its event listings if an author program interests you.
cards.short_summary: An independent bookstore directly across from the downtown train station.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest Book Store is located at 662 North Western Avenue, across from the Lake Forest train station, and hosts author events and book reviews.
cards.access_notes: Open to shoppers during posted business hours; browsing requires no stated reservation, while purchases are optional.

cards.title: Inspect the Pastry Case
cards.subtitle: North Western Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Continue north on Western Avenue and look through the bakery’s pastry case for breads, croissants, tarts, cookies, cakes, or chocolates before ordering.
cards.short_summary: A long-running pastry shop that adds a bakery stop to the Western Avenue walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Gerhard’s operates at 720 North Western Avenue and offers pastries, breads, rolls, croissants, tarts, cookies, cakes, and chocolates.
cards.access_notes: Visit during posted bakery hours; a purchase is required to consume food or beverages.

cards.title: Pause at an All-Day Café
cards.subtitle: East Wisconsin Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Turn onto East Wisconsin Avenue for a café pause, using the official menu to choose among coffee, tea, smoothies, bowls, and other daytime options.
cards.short_summary: A daylight café destination on the Wisconsin Avenue side of downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Hometown Coffee & Juice lists its Lake Forest café at 231 East Wisconsin Avenue and describes coffee, tea, smoothies, and smoothie bowls among its offerings.
cards.access_notes: The official site lists daily daytime hours; purchasing is required for food or drinks.

cards.title: See a Market Square Sports Shop
cards.subtitle: Market Square beside North Western Avenue
cards.notes: Loop from Western Avenue into Market Square and browse bicycles, footwear, and team-sports equipment at this longstanding independent storefront.
cards.short_summary: A visually distinctive sporting-goods and bicycle stop inside historic Market Square.
cards.evidence_claim: Kiddles Sports is located at 258 Market Square and sells sporting goods and bicycles while providing bicycle service and custom apparel.
cards.access_notes: Open to shoppers during posted store hours; purchases and repair services carry costs.
